name: GOTRAX
description: American electric-mobility brand based in Texas, founded in 2017, selling electric scooters, e-bikes, hoverboards and rideables direct to consumers.

evidence.summary: GOTRAX's Awin merchant profile (US programme) states a 5% commission across all categories, an average order value over $350 and a 30-day cookie window.
The same Awin profile publishes jeffl@gotrax.com as the programme's affiliate contact.
The Awin profile describes GOTRAX as an American company based in Texas, operating since 2017, selling electric scooters, bikes and hoverboards.

reasons.niche_fit: Electric scooters and e-bikes are highly demonstrable products that fit tech, commuting and outdoor creator content.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme runs on Awin, a network open to content publishers, but no dedicated creator programme page was found on the brand's own site.
reasons.compensation: 5% is modest as a percentage, but the profiled average order value is over $350, so per-sale payouts are meaningful; no earnings cap is stated, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate contact email (jeffl@gotrax.com) is published on the network profile.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through the Awin network profile.
reasons.credibility: US company trading since 2017 with an established Awin programme and high-ticket products.

name: ENGWE
description: Electric bike brand selling folding, fat-tire and commuter e-bikes in more than 80 countries, with an own affiliate programme run on GoAffPro.

evidence.summary: ENGWE's own affiliate page states affiliates earn 5% of the eligible order amount (excluding taxes and shipping), with a 30-day cookie window; commission becomes payable if the order is not returned within 40 days and is paid around the 10th of the second month via PayPal or bank.
The page states the programme is run through GoAffPro ('Sign up for the ENGWE GoAffPro Affiliate Program') and offers partners a unique link plus discount code.

The page states ENGWE already works with 10,000+ affiliate partners across 80+ countries and offers 1-on-1 dedicated support - an absolute partner count far above the ~100 scale, so saturation is recorded as high rather than low.

reasons.niche_fit: E-bikes are a strong fit for tech-review, commuting and outdoor creators; high prices make single conversions valuable.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own page is built around partners sharing links and codes with their audiences, with dedicated 1-on-1 support.
reasons.compensation: 5% of the eligible order amount on high-ticket e-bikes; no earnings cap is stated anywhere on the page, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application is via the brand's own programme page; no public affiliate email is published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve signup through GoAffPro on the brand's site.
reasons.credibility: Established international e-bike seller operating in 80+ countries, though a younger brand than legacy bike names.

name: Apollo Scooters
description: Canadian electric scooter brand selling performance commuter scooters, running an application-based Affiliate & Creator Program for reviewers, vloggers and creators.

evidence.summary: Apollo's own affiliate registration page describes the 'Apollo Affiliate & Creator Program': commission is a flat rate per item - $4 on non-scooter orders and a flat rate on scooters (amount not stated) - applications are reviewed rather than auto-approved, and affiliates invoice monthly.

Regional versions and third-party listings conflict on pay: the Canadian registration variant quotes 4% of sale and Shopper lists 8%, against the US page's flat-rate-per-item structure, so no single commission rate could be verified and the rate is recorded as null.

An UpPromote case study on Apollo reports two affiliate contribution tiers and 1,000+ affiliates, with affiliate sales making up 15-20% of revenue - a four-figure affiliate count, so saturation is not low.

reasons.niche_fit: Performance e-scooters are a natural fit for tech-review and urban-mobility creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme is explicitly branded an 'Affiliate & Creator Program' and the brand recruits reviewers and vloggers, with a published case study on its affiliate channel.
reasons.compensation: Pay is a flat rate per item ($4 on non-scooter orders; the scooter amount is not published) and regional pages conflict (4% in Canada, 8% in one listing), so no rate is recorded and compensation scores low.
reasons.contact_access: Access is through the brand's own application form; no public partnerships email was found.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application-based with manual approval and monthly self-invoicing, which adds friction versus instant network programmes.
reasons.credibility: Established Canadian scooter brand with a documented, revenue-bearing affiliate programme.

name: Amazfit
description: Smart wearables brand owned by Zepp Health (NYSE: ZEPP) selling smartwatches, fitness bands, the Helio Ring and smart earbuds for sport, health and everyday use.

evidence.summary: Amazfit's official affiliate page states the programme runs on the Impact platform (its 'Apply Here' button links to app.impact.com), with a 30-day cookie window and access to banners, links and product feeds.

The official page's FAQ declines to publish a rate, saying only that commissions are 'generous and attractive'; third-party figures conflict (Lasso 4-8%, an older CJ listing text quoting 4%, an AvantLink listing quoting 10%), so the commission rate is recorded as null.
The page publishes affiliates@zepp.com as the contact for programme questions.
Amazfit's own US blog previously routed applications through CJ, indicating the programme has migrated networks over time; the current official affiliate page routes through Impact.

reasons.niche_fit: Smartwatches and wearables are a core tech/fitness creator category with constant review and comparison demand.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official page explicitly recruits tech, wellness and sports content creators, trainers and recommendation sites.
reasons.compensation: The brand publishes no rate and third-party figures conflict (4%, 4-8% and 10% all circulate), so compensation cannot be verified and scores low.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated affiliate email (affiliates@zepp.com) is published on the official programme page.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application via Impact from the brand's own affiliate page.
reasons.credibility: Owned by NYSE-listed Zepp Health; the brand states it is among the global top 3 in smartwatch shipment volume.

name: HoverAir
description: Maker of the HOVERAir X1 family of self-flying cameras - pocket-sized autonomous drones (X1, X1 PRO, X1 PROMAX) built for hands-free content capture.

evidence.summary: HOVERAir's official affiliate programme page states affiliates earn 5%-8% commission per order with a 30-day cookie duration, on the X1, X1 PRO and X1 PROMAX, joining through the brand's partner platforms.
The brand's global affiliates page lists affiliate@thehover.com as the contact for its affiliate team.

reasons.niche_fit: A self-flying camera is a creator-native product - it exists to make content - so fit for tech, travel and action creators is high.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The official programme page invites affiliates to share the product with their audiences, and the brand actively recruits creators for new models.
reasons.compensation: The brand publishes a 5%-8% per-order range; the recorded rate is the 5% base of that range. No earnings cap is stated, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: An affiliate team email (affiliate@thehover.com) is published on the brand's global affiliates page.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open joining route through the brand's listed partner platforms.
reasons.credibility: Established flying-camera brand with three generations of X1 hardware sold globally.

name: Dalstrong
description: Toronto-founded culinary tools brand (est. 2014) selling knives, knife sets and cookware - 500+ products from $30 to $600 - to professional chefs, home cooks and collectors.

evidence.summary: Dalstrong's own affiliate page states a 10% baseline commission, a 30-day cookie duration, fast payouts, an average order value of $160 and 500+ products priced $30-$600; signup is via its GoAffPro portal (dalstrong.goaffpro.com).
The same page publishes veronica@dalstrong.com for affiliate enquiries and promises creative assets, brand materials and content ideas from a dedicated in-house team.
The page states Dalstrong has sold more than one million products since launching in 2014 and holds 15,000+ five-star reviews, with a 70-day money-back guarantee and lifetime warranty.
Dalstrong's own site states the company was founded in 2014 by David Dallaire and is based in Toronto, Canada.

reasons.niche_fit: Knives and cookware are staple demo products for food, cooking and kitchen creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand supplies creative assets, content ideas and an affiliate community, and markets the programme to its 'million-strong' audience of cooks and collectors.
reasons.compensation: 10% baseline commission on a $160 average order with fast payouts is strong for the home niche; no earnings cap is stated, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate contact email is published on the programme page alongside open signup.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open self-serve application through the brand's GoAffPro portal.
reasons.credibility: Trading since 2014 with 1M+ products sold and 15,000+ five-star reviews.

name: Hedgehog Dryer
description: Norwegian home-appliance brand (founded 2019) making fast, design-award-winning dryers for shoes, boots and gloves, sold through retailers including Lowe's in the US.

evidence.summary: Hedgehog Dryer's own US affiliate page states: 'There is no cap to what you can earn in the Hedgehog Dryer affiliate program' and 'Start earning unlimited commissions for every customer you bring us' - an explicit no-earnings-cap statement, so the commission cap is recorded as uncapped.

The same page states the programme currently offers 10% commissions on all products (negotiable upward for consistent sellers and influencers) and that affiliates register on the Awin network or the AvantLink platform, with a dedicated affiliate manager.
BusinessWire reports Hedgehog Dryer was founded in 2019 in Norway by Bjorn Holte, holds four design awards, and launched in the US with Lowe's.

reasons.niche_fit: A single-purpose home appliance - a strong seasonal fit for family, ski, outdoor and home-hack creators rather than a broad home niche play.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme page names social media influencers as a group that can earn raised rates, but shows no dedicated creator content programme.
reasons.compensation: 10% on all products with an explicitly uncapped earnings statement on the brand's own page, and rates negotiable upward - the strongest verified compensation terms in this batch.
reasons.contact_access: Signup is via Awin or AvantLink from the brand page; support is via a dedicated affiliate manager, but no public email is published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free, open registration through two major networks.
reasons.credibility: Founded 2019 in Norway, Red Dot and TIME Best Inventions recognition, and US retail distribution through Lowe's.

name: Zooplus
description: Europe's largest online pet retailer by sales, operating in 21 markets with around 9,840 pet food and accessory products; this entry covers its UK storefront programme on Awin.

evidence.summary: Zooplus's Awin merchant profile (UK programme) states commission of 7% on a customer's first 3 orders and 1% from the 4th order onwards, with an average order value of GBP 46.
The Awin profile explicitly invites influencer, content creator and pet community publisher types to the programme.
The profile describes Zooplus as Europe's number one online pet retailer by sales, active in 21 markets with 9,840 products.

reasons.niche_fit: A full-range pet supplies retailer gives pet creators an almost unlimited product pool to feature.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The network profile explicitly recruits influencers, content creators and pet communities, not just coupon sites.
reasons.compensation: 7% applies to a customer's first 3 orders before dropping to 1%, so earnings are front-loaded; the recorded rate is the 7% headline. No cap is stated, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Contact is through the Awin network only; no public affiliate email was found.
reasons.credibility: Europe's largest online pet retailer by sales, operating across 21 markets.

name: Lily's Kitchen
description: UK natural pet food brand making nutritionally complete wet and dry food, treats and chews for dogs and cats with natural ingredients.

evidence.summary: Lily's Kitchen's Awin merchant profile states commission of 5% on new customers and 2% on existing customers (voucher-code affiliates 2% new / 1% existing), an average order value over GBP 50, a 30-day cookie, and rates excluding VAT and delivery.
The profile presents Lily's Kitchen as a UK natural pet food brand for dogs and cats.

reasons.niche_fit: Premium natural pet food is a core, repeat-purchase category for dog and cat creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The programme is open to content publishers via Awin, though the profile shows no creator-specific perks.
reasons.compensation: 5% on new customers (2% existing) over a GBP 50+ average order is mid-range for pet food; the recorded rate is the 5% new-customer rate. No cap is stated, so the cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Contact is through the Awin network only; no public affiliate email was found.
reasons.credibility: Long-established UK premium pet food brand with national retail presence.

name: Pets at Home
description: The UK's leading pet care retailer, selling pet food, accessories and services online and through its national store network, with a large affiliate programme run on Rakuten Advertising.

evidence.summary: A Rakuten Advertising case study states Pets at Home uses Rakuten Advertising as its affiliate network of choice, running a diversified full-funnel programme including content publishers, with affiliate sales up 52% year on year.
The same case study describes Pets at Home as the UK's leading pet care retailer.

No commission rate is published in the Rakuten case study or on a public programme page; the only figure circulating is an unreliable sub-network listing (up to 0.6%), so the rate is recorded as null.

opportunity.title: Pets at Home Affiliate Programme (Rakuten Advertising)

reasons.niche_fit: The UK's biggest pet retailer covers every pet category a creator might feature.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Rakuten's case study confirms content publishers are an active part of the programme's publisher mix.
reasons.compensation: No commission rate is published anywhere public, so compensation cannot be verified and scores at the floor for an established programme.
reasons.contact_access: Access is managed through the Rakuten network; no public affiliate contact was found.
reasons.opportunity_availability: A large, actively managed programme, but joining is via network application and approval rather than an open brand page.
reasons.credibility: The UK's leading pet care retailer with a documented, fast-growing affiliate channel.
